merger_description:
Thoma Bravo L.P. (**Thoma Bravo**), is one of the largest software-focused investors in the world, with approximately USD 170 billion in assets under management as of June 30, 2026. Through its private equity, growth equity and credit strategies, the firm invests in companies operating in the software and technology sectors. Over the past 20+ years, the firm has acquired or invested in approximately 600 companies representing approximately USD 325 billion in enterprise value (including control and non-control investments).

Accelerant Holdings (**Accelerant**) operates a data-driven risk exchange that connects specialty insurance underwriters, including Managing General Agents with insurers, reinsurers and other providers of risk capital through an AI-driven technology and data platform. Accelerant is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: ARX).

Altamont Capital Partners (**Altamont**) is a private equity firm focused on transforming and scaling lower-middle-market companies across the Financial Services, Industrials and Business Services sectors. Altamont has invested in over 50 companies and currently manages over $4 billion of capital. Altamont is Accelerant’s largest investor.

Funds managed by Thoma Bravo, acting through affiliated acquisition vehicles, propose to acquire up to 100% of the capital in Accelerant (the **Acquisition**). The Acquisition involves the take-private of Accelerant.

Altamont Capital Partners and Accelerant Holdings’ founders intend to retain a degree of equity ownership alongside Thoma Bravo, with the terms to be finalised prior to closing.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between Thoma Bravo (and its
connected entities) and Accelerant in the supply of specialty
insurance risk exchange platform services or the supply of
specialty litigation insurance products
b. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
